title: ddPCR
author: Lele Sun

steps_raw.instruction: 1- Wear clean gloves;
2- Clean pipettes and stand with 75% alcohol;
3- Thaw DNA samples and all reagents ((2× ddPCR Supermix for Probes (no dUTP; Bio-Rad, catalog: 1863024), primers (10μM) and probes (10μM));
4- Gently mix the DNA samples and mix thoroughly the reagents on the vortex.
5- Centrifuge the DNA samples and reagents with a spin;
6- Keep reagents on ice;
7- Label the microtubes and leave them ready for preparation of the mix.
8- Required equipment: QX200TM Droplet Generator, QX200TM Droplet Reader, PX1TM PCR Plate Sealer, Applied Biosystems™ Thermal Cycler (Veriti 96 well);

9- Required consumables: Droplet Generation Oil (Catalog: 1863005), ddPCR™ Droplet Reader Oil (Catalog:1863004), DG8™ Cartridges (Catalog: 1864008), DG8™ Gaskets (Catalog: 1863009), 96 plates (Catalog: 12001925).

1- Prepare the reaction mix for the number of reactions needed according to the guidelines in the Table 1. Assemble all required components except the sample, dispense equal aliquots into each reaction tube, and add the sample to each reactions tube as the final step.
Table 1. Preparation of the reaction mix.
2- Mix thoroughly the tubes on the vortex, and centrifuge briefly with a spin.

3- Once the reaction mixture are ready, load 20 μl of each reaction mix into a sample well of a DG8™ Cartridge for QX200TM Droplet Generator followed by 70μl of Droplet Generation Oil into the oil wells. For the Automated Droplet Generator, follow instructions in the Automated Droplet Generator instruction manual.
Themal Cycling Conditions
1- After droplet generation with the QX200TM Droplet Generator, carefully transfer droplets into a clean 96-well plate. Seal the plate with the PX1 PCR Plate Sealer.
2- Proceed to thermal cycling ( Table 2) and subsequent reading of droplets in the QX200TM Droplet Reader.
Table 2. Thermal cycling conditions.
Data Acquisition and Analysis
1- After themal cycling, place the sealed 96-well plate in the QX200TM Droplet Reader.
2- Open QuantaSoft software version 1.7.4 (Bio-Rad) to set up a new plate layout and run according to the QuantaSoft software version 1.7.4 instruction manual.
3- After data acquisition, set thresholds manually (RLEP for 5000 and groEL for 2500).

4- A positive well was defined if more than 4 fluorescent signal events were shown above the threshold line. The test sample was positive when the four test wells (RLEP and groEL in duplicate) showed at least 3 positive wells.
Component | Volume per reaction, μl | Final concentration
2× ddPCR Supermix for Probes | 10 | 1×
(10μM) Forward primer | 1.8 | 900nM
(10μM) Reverse primer | 1.8 | 900nM
(10μM) Probes | 0.5 | 250nM
RNase-/DNase-free water | 1.9
Cycling Step | Temperature, ℃ | Time | Ramp Rate | Number of Cycles
Enzyme activation | 95 | 10min | 2℃/sec | 1
Denaturation | 94 | 30sec | 2℃/sec | 40
Annealing/extension | 60 | 60sec | 2℃/sec | 40
Enzyme deactivation | 98 | 5min | 2℃/sec | 1
Hold | 16 | 2℃/sec | 1
